blogs.title: The Paradoxical Breath: Recognizing Acquired Central Hypoventilation in the Absence of Air Hunger
blogs.description: Explore the unique clinical presentation of Chiari malformation type I (CMI) where patients experience profound desaturation without true dyspnea. Discuss the neurophysiology of 'air hunger,' and learn to spot this benign-but-fatally-dangerous sign of brainstem compression in primary care and ED settings.

blogs.title: When the Swallow Fails but the Scope Passes: Neurogenic Dysphagia and the CMI Red Flags
blogs.description: Analyze the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing neurogenic from mechanical dysphagia. Highlight key historical clues (solids/liquids simultaneously, 14-year delay) that suggest underlying structural brainstem pathology despite normal endoscopic evaluation.

blogs.title: The Archive is the Best Tool: Why 14-Year-Old CT Scans Matter in Adult Onset Neurology
blogs.description: Address the case of the overlooked foramen magnum on old trauma imaging. Provide a clinical strategy for reviewing archival imaging when new scanners show significant changes and discuss the utility of detecting static structural pathology on outdated medium-resolution scans.

blogs.title: Scalp Sensitivity as a Neurological Signal: Vertex Allodynia in Chiari Malformation
blogs.description: Delve into the specific, under-recognized symptom of vertex headache and cutaneous allodynia in CMI. Analyze the relief of symptoms via hair cutting as a diagnostic marker and contrast this with common occipital neuralgia presentations.

blogs.title: Beyond the AHI: Interpreting Sleep Studies in Central Sleep Apnea and Constraint
blogs.description: Critique the limitations of Type III sleep studies versus full Type I polysomnography in diagnosing central hypoventilation syndromes. Discuss why an apnea-hypopnea index of 6.0 cannot be trusted in CMI patients without EEG and video monitoring.
